title: Power and energy transfer rate practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All seven contexts, values, prompts and the visual brief are original. They reproduce lesson demand patterns without copying official wording, values or diagram geometry.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by work done and give the equation for work done by a constant force acting in the direction of motion.
A machine transfers 600 J of energy in 3.0 s. What is its average power?
Which statement about a device rated at 75 W is correct?

options.B: It transfers 75 J of energy every second while operating at that power.
options.C: It transfers 75 J of energy in every minute.
options.D: It must transfer more total energy than every lower-power device.

questions.prompt: Machine X transfers 12 kJ in 40 s. Machine Y transfers 9.0 kJ in 20 s. Which comparison is correct?

options.A: X has greater power because it transfers more energy.
options.B: X has greater power because it operates for longer.
options.C: Y has greater power because 450 W is greater than 300 W.
options.D: They have equal power because both energies are measured in kilojoules.

questions.prompt: A workshop hoist transfers 3.6 kJ of energy while lifting each crate. It lifts 12 crates in 90 s.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total energy transferred while the 12 crates are lifted.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average power of the hoist during the 90 s interval.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State what the calculated power means in terms of energy transferred each second.

questions.prompt: An energy store decreases from 540 kJ to 180 kJ during 2.5 h of operation. Assume the average transfer rate remains the same for the later interval in part (b).

figure.purpose: Support careful reading of an energy decrease and a long time conversion without being required to answer the text-complete question.
figure.brief: Landscape 3:2 original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired line diagram. Draw a left energy bar labelled initial 540 kJ, a right shorter bar labelled final 180 kJ, and a clean time bracket labelled 2.5 h. Do not show the energy difference, converted time, formula, power or any answer.
figure.alt_text: An energy store decreases from 540 kilojoules to 180 kilojoules over 2.5 hours.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average power transferred from the store during the 2.5 h interval.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the additional time needed to transfer 90 kJ at the same average power.

questions.prompt: A horizontal tow cable exerts a constant force of 1.8 kN on a platform. The platform moves 32 m in the direction of the force during 48 s.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the cable.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use your answer to (a) to calculate the average power transferred by the cable.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A second tow completes the same work in 36 s. Calculate its average power.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain why the second tow has greater power although the work done is unchanged.
